steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Ore
form.label: a few grams in every tonne

steps.text: The six platinum-group metals occur together. Most lie in a few thin layers of the Bushveld Complex in South Africa, an ancient body of once-molten rock, with more in Zimbabwe's Great Dyke. In Russia and Canada they come as a by-product of nickel and copper sulphide ore. Rhodium is a small fraction of the mix, richest in South Africa's UG2 reef.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: The South African reefs are about a metre thick and are followed more than a kilometre underground. Miners drill and blast the narrow seam and haul the rock to the shaft. It is deep, hot and labour-intensive work.

steps.title: Concentrate
steps.text: The ore is milled to powder and floated. The platinum-group metals follow the nickel and copper sulphide grains into a concentrate that is a small fraction of the rock mined.

steps.title: Smelt
steps.text: An electric furnace melts the concentrate. Silicates leave as slag and the metals collect in a matte of nickel, copper and iron sulphide. A converter burns off the iron. The nickel and copper are then leached away for sale, leaving a residue rich in precious metals.

steps.title: Refine
steps.text: The residue is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and chlorine. One by one the metals are pulled out by solvent extraction, precipitation and distillation, in a refinery where material can spend weeks or months. Rhodium is one of the minor metals, recovered late from what platinum and palladium leave behind.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Rhodium powder is dissolved into salts and coated, with platinum or palladium, onto the ceramic honeycomb of catalytic converters. Some is alloyed with platinum for glass-making equipment and thermocouples.
steps.india: Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India with imported metal.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Nearly all rhodium goes into catalytic converters, where it is the metal that breaks down nitrogen oxides. Nothing else does that job as well, so a small market swings widely in price. Chemical plants use it to make acetic acid.
steps.india: All primary metal is imported, for vehicle and chemical catalysts.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Scrapped catalytic converters are the only large source outside the mines, and rhodium is refined out of them together with platinum and palladium.
steps.india: Hindustan Platinum and other refiners recover platinum-group metals from spent catalysts. A Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme (2025) covers catalytic converters.
